title: Make a card payment all or nothing

blocks.text: The wallet service takes card payments in two steps: it debits the wallet, then inserts a payment row whose `reference` column holds at most 16 characters. Support has three tickets this week. A merchant sent a 19-character invoice number, the payment failed, and the customer's wallet was short by the amount anyway. A payment request with a mistyped wallet id "succeeded" and left a payment row for a wallet that doesn't exist. And after a failed payment, a later request on the same pooled connection saved a profile change that no other server ever saw.

Write `pay(connection, wallet, amount, reference)` in `src/main/java/practice/Payments.java`, using the existing `debit(...)` and `record(...)`. A payment either debits and records, or changes nothing and throws `SQLException`. The connection is lent by the request handler, which goes on using it afterwards in the mode it had before the call. About twelve lines.

cases.says: a payment debits the wallet and records a payment row, both visible to another session
several payments in a row on the same connection all take effect
when the payment row is rejected, the SQLException reaches the caller and the wallet keeps its balance, as seen from the same connection and from another
after a failed payment the lent connection is back in auto-commit mode, so the caller's next statement commits
a payment from a wallet id that matches no row throws SQLException and records nothing

origin.section: Auto-Commit Is On, So Each Statement Commits by Itself

concepts: Changing the auto-commit mode during a transaction commits it, so a finally that restores the mode without a rollback commits the half-done work.
Turning auto-commit off, committing at the end, rolling back in the catch and restoring the mode makes the statements all or nothing.
executeUpdate and executeBatch return how many rows each statement changed, and 0 means the WHERE matched nothing, not an error.
